findings.evidence: The libc allow-list skip is anchored `^[[:space:]]*@preconcurrency ...import` in k07.sh:75, checks/weaken-check.sh:45 and the hatch-delta awk at swift-quality.md:135. vapor/console-kit writes the chain as `@unsafe @preconcurrency [public] import Glibc|Musl|Android` (21 lines in 7 files, tools 6.2 with strictMemorySafety, which SW-SEC-11 recommends). `bash k07.sh` in a console-kit copy exits 1 and prints all 21 lines. Plant on a branch: `@unsafe @preconcurrency import Glibc` makes weaken-check.sh exit 1 and the hatch-delta awk print it, while plain `@preconcurrency import Glibc` is skipped. concurrency.md:173 S2 (prefix accepted via `sub(/.*@preconcurrency/...)`) is empty on the same tree, so the checks disagree.
findings.fix: Allow leading attributes in all three skips: `^[+]?[[:space:]]*(@[A-Za-z_]+[[:space:]]+)*@preconcurrency...`. Add the `@unsafe` form to the right-hand example in language.md and run all four checks over it.

findings.evidence: The MUST row's e-greps first command (`-e ': RandomNumberGenerator'`, empty output = pass) matches a generic constraint that takes a generator. swift-numerics Sources/_TestSupport/RealTestSupport.swift:30 `static func random<G: RandomNumberGenerator>(using g: inout G)` prints. That is the `using: &g` shape the row itself prescribes, not a custom generator. Other hits on the three trees: none.
findings.fix: Narrow the pattern to conformers: `(struct|class|enum|actor|extension)[^{]*:[^{]*RandomNumberGenerator`. Keep the libc names as they are and add a generic-parameter twin to the watched-green set.

findings.evidence: The G4 cells grep every file with `@main` under Sources, not the executable-target list that the G0 block builds from dump-package. pointfreeco/swift-case-paths has no executable target (G0 prints 'no executable target, SW-CLI does not apply'), yet G4-08, G4-23 and G4-25 each print Sources/CasePathsMacros/Plugin.swift (`@main struct CasePathsPlugin: CompilerPlugin`, a macro plugin that never touches argv or stdout). console-kit prints the example executable Sources/ConsoleLoggerExample/entrypoint.swift while the G1 block skips `*Example` dirs. The rows say they bind every `@main` executable.
findings.fix: Run the G4 greps over the same DIRS array as G1, behind the same G0 guard, or exclude `CompilerPlugin` conformers. Say in the index that a macro plugin is not a CLI.

findings.evidence: Step 10's sha-pin line is `grep -rn -e 'uses: ' ... | grep -v -e 'uses: \./' | grep -v -E -e '@[0-9a-f]{40}'`. rules/swift-package/gates.md:275 has the same pipeline plus `-e '^[^:]*:[0-9]+: *#'`. The restated command is weaker than the owner block.
findings.fix: Copy the comment exclusion from gates.md:275 into step 10, or point step 10 at the gates.md block instead of restating it.

findings.evidence: P10 runs `grep -rn --include='Package.swift' ... -e '.package(path:' -e 'branch:' -e 'revision:' .` over the whole tree. console-kit prints ./Benchmarks/Package.swift:10 `.package(path: "../")`, a nested Benchmarks fixture manifest that is no product. SW-PKG-20's own cell restricts to `-maxdepth 1` and says why. SKILL.md step 3 sends every library to P10, so a library with a Benchmarks package fails the release scan. P10 also reads `branch:` inside comments.
findings.fix: Use `find . -maxdepth 1 -name 'Package*.swift' -exec grep -Hn ... {} +` with `^[^/]*` comment skipping, as SW-PKG-20 does.

findings.evidence: `find . -name 'Package.swift'` has no depth limit. On console-kit it exits 1 with 7 lines from ./Benchmarks/Package.swift (a fixture manifest, duplicates included) beside the 7 lines of the root manifest's shared `swiftSettings` array. The header documents the shared-array print but not the nested manifest.
findings.fix: Add `-maxdepth 1` (root manifests only), or exclude Benchmarks, Tests and Examples manifests as SW-PKG-20 does.

findings.evidence: Step 2 declares `.claude` and `.agents` 'not dirt' and the skill requires the rule set installed in `.claude/`. SwiftPM's SBOM counts untracked files. Plant (tagged v1.0.0, clean tree): SBOM version `v1.0.0`. After `mkdir .claude; echo x > .claude/note` (git status `?? .claude/`): `cyclonedx1-1.7-tool-v1.0.0-modified-all-...json`. Step 8's `grep -L -F -e " : \"$TAG\""` then lists it as a finding. With `.claude/` in .git/info/exclude the SBOM is `v1.0.0` again. A literal run reaches step 8 with a state that step 2 called clean and step 8 cannot pass. My console-kit run printed `v1.2.3-modified` the same way.
findings.fix: Add a step 2 line `printf '.claude/\n.agents/\n' >> .git/info/exclude` (or build from a clean `git worktree`), and state that the exclusion is what makes the SBOM tag exact.

findings.evidence: The pin-grep (swift-quality.md:131) and the U1 inventory only match `swift:[0-9]`, `matrix.swift` and a `swift:` key. SW-GATE-24 (gates.md:270) requires `linux_swift_versions` to be passed explicitly to swiftlang/github-workflows. Plant `.github/workflows/pr.yml` with `linux_swift_versions: '["6.2", "6.3", "6.4"]'`: the U1 grep exits 1 with no output, so U1 reads 'no literal tag' and never derives or reports those legs. swift-numerics' only CI is that reusable workflow with no version input.
findings.fix: Add `-e 'swift_versions:'` and `-e 'swift_version:'` to the pin-grep and U1 inventory, and say that a reusable-workflow input list is a leg that U1 reads by hand.

findings.known_class: procedure step assumes preconditions it never establishes
findings.evidence: U2 says 'Move every shared setting into the one `for target in package.targets` loop' and 'Add .treatWarning ... to that loop', and U6/U9 refer to 'the loop'. swift-numerics (tools 5.9, per-target literals) and case-paths have no such loop. The skill never says to create it (the shape is only in rules/swift-package.md:154). My dry-run reached U8 with `migrate` writing per-target literals and no loop. A C target does build with the loop (checked on a C+Swift plant).
findings.fix: One sentence in U2: if no loop exists, add the one from SW-PKG-18's example, then move the shared settings into it.

findings.evidence: The row allows `precondition` with `// invariant:` or a `- Precondition:` doc line. The G4 cell only filters `grep -v -e 'invariant:'`. Plant `/// - Precondition: n > 0` over `precondition(n > 0)` prints `Sources/A/a.swift:4:  precondition(n > 0)`. The row concedes the doc-line half was not watched. It also prints a `///` prose line (swift-numerics Polar.swift:115).
findings.fix: Make the filter context-aware (awk: skip when one of the 3 lines above has `- Precondition:`) or demote the cell to an inventory.

findings.evidence: G2-15a/d hard-code `Sources/App`. On swift-numerics, case-paths and console-kit the cell prints `grep: Sources/App: No such file or directory` and the pipeline into awk hides the status, so rc=0 reads as pass. G2-15a also excludes `App`, so a non-Vapor server layout is never scanned.
findings.fix: Take the entry-target directory from the DIRS array of G0, or guard with `[ -d Sources/App ]` and print 'G2-15: no Sources/App, name the entry target'.

findings.evidence: Step 3's second line `diagnose-api-breaking-changes "$LAST" 2>&1 | grep -e 'breaking change' -e 'get revision'` is said to tell apart the two exit-1 causes. On a clean library (console-kit rel-ck vs v1.0.0, exit 0) it prints `No breaking changes detected in ConsoleKit` and `...in ConsoleLogger`, because 'breaking change' is a substring of the pass message. A literal reader sees a hit on a pass, and the pipeline's own exit is grep's. It also runs the whole baseline diagnosis twice. `--scratch-path` placed after the subcommand exits 64 (`Unknown option`), so a scratch-path variant of the line needs it before the subcommand.
findings.fix: Run once into a log, then `grep -e '[1-9][0-9]* breaking change' -e 'get revision' "$LOG"` only when the exit is non-zero. Show `swift package --scratch-path DIR diagnose-api-breaking-changes TAG` if a scratch path is wanted.
